ground_truth_witness: The witness is the exact evaluation of the printed expression itself. With standard binomial coefficients: C(0,2) = 0, C(6,2) = 15, C(5,2) = 10, C(0,2) = 0, so the left-hand side is 0 + 19*15 + 10 + 99*0 = 0 + 285 + 10 + 0 = 295. The proof asserts this equals 310; in fact it equals 295, an error of 15. Robustness sweep: all 2^4 = 16 argument-order readings of the four terse \binom a b tokens, crossed with 2 binomial conventions (standard, with C(n,k)=0 for k>n, and the generalized falling-factorial C(n,k)=n(n-1)...(n-k+1)/k!), yield only the values {0, 1, 10, 11, 99, 100, 109, 110, 285, 286, 295, 296, 384, 385, 394, 395}; none is 310. A single-token perturbation sweep shows the only ways to reach 310 by changing one printed token are multiplier 19 -> 20 (20*15 + 10 = 310) or the first term's upper argument 0 -> 6, suggesting an off-by-one coefficient in the worked example, but the line as printed is false.
ground_truth_flaw: In the author's own worked example, the day-2 value of the monovariant is asserted to be S = \binom 02 + 19\cdot\binom 62 + \binom 52 + 99\cdot\binom 02 = 310. The stated sum is arithmetically false: the listed terms evaluate to 295, not 310.
